Use a theme
Apply a theme to your app: install, import with the CLI, wire the generated module, switch dark mode, nest themes, and
choose runtime or built for production.

package: @astryxdesign/cli

quick-start                     Wrap your app in a theme - `theme add` records an installed package theme and
                                regenerates `src/astryx-themes.ts` or `.js` with its built module, production CSS, and
                                optional font CSS. In a project without `src`, the module is at the project root. The
                                first imported...
migrating-earlier-theme-copies  Migrating Earlier Theme Copies - A theme copied by the released `theme add` stays app
                                source. The upgrade does not move, delete, or rewrite it. It only writes the missing
                                same-stem descriptor with `maintained: false`, so the copy becomes a local theme.
available-themes                Available Themes - Install the theme package you want with `npm install
                                @astryxdesign/theme-<name>`, then import its slug with `theme add <slug>`. The CLI
                                imports the package's built outputs for you.
theme-props                     Theme Props - `<Theme>` takes `theme` (required), `mode` (`'system'` by default, or
                                `'light'`/`'dark'`), and `children`. For every prop, run `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12
                                component Theme`.
integration-themes              Using a Theme from an Integration - Install the integration as a direct dependency.
                                Astryx discovers its themes and guides without an `astryx.config` entry. A theme can be
                                added only when the installed package exports its built module and production
                                stylesheet.
light-dark-mode                 Dark mode - Use [light, dark] tuples in token values for automatic mode switching. Use
                                mode='system' (default) on Theme to follow OS preference.
nesting-themes                  Nested themes - Wrap different sections in separate `<Theme>` providers.
runtime-vs-built-themes         Runtime vs Built Themes - Themes work in two modes:

Read one section: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs use-a-theme <section>
Read everything:  npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs use-a-theme --full
